correctness.rationale: For integer m>=2, 0<a<1/m, p=ma and q=1-ma, Lebesgue-invariant center-coordinate Koopman P satisfies P h0=a h0+q h1, P h_k=p h_(k-1)+q h_(k+1) for k>=1, h_k(y)={m^k y}-1/2, with inner products <h0,h_k>=1/(12m^k). In the formal resolvent, r(z) is the zero-constant solution r=qz+pzr², and coefficient functions u_k=r^k/(1-az-pzr). Summing <h0,u_kh_k> gives the claimed Cgf=[12(1-r/m)(1-az-pzr)]^-1. A positive real pole from r=m occurs only at a<1/[m(m²+1)] and a boundary-factor pole only at a>m/(m²+1); at equality each merges with the +R square-root singularity R=(2sqrt(pq))^-1. Expanding at ±R yields n^-3/2 with explicit positive even/odd amplitudes between thresholds, n^-1/2 at either critical threshold, and the two claimed pure exponential pole regimes outside. Independent exact rational recurrence/formal power-series coefficients agree to 29 terms in the assigned checker, and a separate direct rational walk recurrence for m=2,3,4 at interior/exterior a values reproduces initial C0,C1,C2,C3. This is an analytic all-parameter proof; finite checks are diagnostic.
residual_risks: This is a stationary center-coordinate observable, not sharp correlation rates for every Hölder function or arbitrary invariant measures.
At transition parameters, leading asymptotics fix a rather than taking a joint near-critical window.
